mnemonic: NACHT means 'night' — NÄCHTLICH = 'night-ly' → NIGHTLY.

example.en: The campaign is taking place nationwide.

mnemonic: BUND (federation) + WEIT (wide) = 'federation-wide' → NATIONWIDE.

example.de: Mittlerweile hat er die Prüfung bestanden.
example.en: In the meantime, he has passed the exam.

mnemonic: MITTLER (middle) + WEILE (while) = 'in the middle while' → IN THE MEANTIME.
AUSSER (outside) + HALB (half) = 'outside the half [space]' → OUTSIDE.
BEREIT means 'ready' — BEREITS = 'already ready' → ALREADY.

example.de: Bitte antworten Sie innerhalb einer Woche.

mnemonic: INNER (inner) + HALB (half) = 'within the half [space]' → WITHIN.
A casual regional tag-word, like ending a sentence with '...right?' → HUH, RIGHT?
FOLGEND (following) + MASSEN (measures/manner) = 'in the following manner' → AS FOLLOWS.
DAUERN means 'to last' — DAUERND = 'lasting' → CONSTANTLY.

example.de: Ich komme mit, allerdings erst später.
example.en: I'll come along, though only later.

mnemonic: ALLER (of all) + DINGS (things) = 'of all things' → THOUGH, admittedly, still.

example.en: The appointment was cancelled at short notice.

mnemonic: KURZ (short) + FRIST (deadline/period) = 'short period' → SHORT-TERM.

en: to cancel, block, close off, freeze

mnemonic: UM (around) + GEHEND (going) — going around to it right away: IMMEDIATELY.

example.de: Wir haben zwischendurch eine kleine Pause gemacht.
example.en: We took a short break in between.

mnemonic: ZWISCHEN (between) + DURCH (through) = 'through between' → IN BETWEEN, meanwhile.

example.de: Der damalige Bürgermeister hat das Projekt gestartet.
example.en: The then mayor started the project.

mnemonic: DAMALS means 'back then' — DAMALIG is the adjective: FROM THAT TIME, onetime.

example.en: Why are you even doing that?

mnemonic: ÜBER (over) + HAUPT (head/main) = 'over the main point' → AT ALL, in general.

example.de: Welche Farbe magst du am liebsten?
example.en: Which color do you like best?

example.de: Wir planen eine Reise nach Italien.
example.en: We're planning a trip to Italy.

en: to know how to go on

mnemonic: ENDE means 'end' — ENDLICH is reaching the END at last: FINALLY.

example.en: Take this chair as a substitute.

mnemonic: ERSATZ means 'substitute/replacement' — ERSATZWEISE = AS A SUBSTITUTE.

example.de: Der Zug kommt erst um zehn Uhr.
example.en: The train doesn't arrive until ten o'clock.

mnemonic: ERST sounds like 'first' — but it also means NOT UNTIL a certain point.
HER points TOWARD the speaker — 'come HER(e)!' → FROM (toward me).

example.de: Das Haus ist innen ganz renoviert.
example.en: The house is completely renovated on the inside.

mnemonic: IN + -EN — the IN-side of something: INSIDE.

example.de: Wir kamen kurz vor Mitternacht an.

mnemonic: KURZ (short) + VOR (before) = 'shortly before' — a SHORT time before something.

example.de: Ich habe lange auf dich gewartet.
example.en: I waited for you for a long time.

mnemonic: LANG means 'long' — LANGE is the adverb form: FOR A LONG TIME.

example.de: Mitunter regnet es hier im Sommer.
example.en: Occasionally it rains here in summer.

mnemonic: MIT (with) + UNTER (under/among) = 'among with' → OCCASIONALLY, now and then.

example.de: Die Schule ist ganz in der Nähe.
example.en: The school is very close by.

example.de: Ich bin gerade unterwegs zur Arbeit.
example.en: I'm on my way to work right now.

mnemonic: UNTER (under) + WEG (way) = 'under way' → ON THE WAY, traveling.
WAHR (true) + SCHEIN (to seem) + -LICH = 'seeming true' → PROBABLY.

example.de: Das Problem ist zum Teil meine Schuld.
example.en: The problem is partly my fault.

mnemonic: ZUM (to the) + TEIL (part) = 'to the part' → PARTLY, in part.
VOR (forward/before) + WÄRTS (-wards) = FORWARD.

example.de: Du könntest zum Beispiel Deutsch lernen.
example.en: You could, for example, learn German.

mnemonic: ZUM (to the) + BEISPIEL (example) = 'to the example' → FOR EXAMPLE.

example.de: Gib gut Acht auf deine Sachen.
example.en: Pay close attention to your belongings.

mnemonic: ACHT sounds like 'watch' (Ac(h)t) — GIVE (geben) your watchfulness: PAY ATTENTION.

example.en: All the best for your birthday!

mnemonic: ALLES (everything) + GUTE (good) = 'everything good' → ALL THE BEST.

example.de: Also gut, wir machen es so.
example.en: Alright then, we'll do it that way.

mnemonic: ALSO (so/well) + GUT (good) = 'so, good' → ALRIGHT THEN, giving consent.
AN (at) + VORBEI (past) — picture walking right AT something and going PAST it.
AUSSER (outside of) + HAUS (house) = 'outside the house' → takeout, not eating in.

example.de: Die Fabrik liegt außerhalb von der Stadt.
example.en: The factory is located outside of the city.

mnemonic: AUSSER (outside) + HALB (half) + VON (of) = 'outside the halved space' → OUTSIDE OF.

example.de: Ich bin krank, d. h. ich kann nicht kommen.
example.en: I'm sick, that is, I can't come.

mnemonic: Short for 'das heißt' (that means) — abbreviation for 'THAT IS / i.e.'.

example.de: Ich war müde, deshalb bin ich früh ins Bett gegangen.
example.en: I was tired, so I went to bed early.

mnemonic: DES (of this) + HALB (half/reason) = 'for this reason' → THEREFORE.
ERST (first) + MAL (time) = 'first time/round' → FIRST OF ALL, to begin with.

example.de: Das Café ist gegenüber von der Post.
example.en: The café is opposite the post office.

mnemonic: GEGEN (against) + ÜBER (over) + VON (of) = 'facing across from' → OPPOSITE of.

example.de: Ein Ticket hin und zurück, bitte.

mnemonic: HIN (there) + UND (and) + ZURÜCK (back) = 'there and back' → ROUND TRIP.
HIN (toward/away) + UNTER (under/down) = 'away downward' → DOWN.
IN + ORDNUNG (order) = 'in order' → OKAY, everything fine.

example.de: In Zukunft möchte ich mehr sparen.
example.en: In the future, I'd like to save more.

mnemonic: IN + ZUKUNFT (future) = literally 'in the future'.
MEHR (more) + MALS (times) = 'more times' → SEVERAL TIMES.

example.de: Das Hotel liegt mitten in der Stadt.
example.en: The hotel is right in the middle of the city.

mnemonic: MITTE means 'middle' — MITTEN is being right IN THE MIDDLE OF something.
NIE (never) + MEHR (more) = 'never more' → NEVER AGAIN.

example.en: Be there by seven at the latest.

mnemonic: SPÄT means 'late' — SPÄTESTENS is the superlative: AT THE LATEST, the latest possible time.

example.en: She works by the hour at the café.

mnemonic: STUNDE (hour) + -WEISE (-wise/manner) = 'hour-wise' → BY THE HOUR.

example.de: Tagsüber ist es hier sehr ruhig.
example.en: It's very quiet here during the day.

mnemonic: TAG (day) + ÜBER (over/across) = 'across the day' → DURING THE DAY.

example.en: A thousand thanks for your help!

mnemonic: TAUSEND (thousand) + DANK (thanks) = 'a thousand thanks' → THANKS A LOT.

example.de: Wir haben unter anderem über die Arbeit gesprochen.
example.en: Among other things, we talked about work.

mnemonic: UNTER (among) + ANDEREM (other things) = 'among other things'.

example.de: Wir brauchen Brot, Milch, Eier usw.
example.en: We need bread, milk, eggs, etc.

mnemonic: Abbreviation for 'und so weiter' (and so further) → ETC., AND SO ON.

example.de: Der Zug fährt von Berlin nach München.
example.en: The train goes from Berlin to Munich.

mnemonic: VON (from) + NACH (to) = literally 'FROM ... TO'.

example.de: Abends lese ich gern ein Buch.
example.en: In the evening I like to read a book.

mnemonic: ABEND means 'evening' — ABENDS = 'evening-ly' → IN THE EVENING.

example.de: Wir kommen auf jeden Fall zur Party.
example.en: We're definitely coming to the party.

mnemonic: AUF (in) + JEDEN (every) + FALL (case) = 'in every case' → DEFINITELY.

example.de: Auf Wiederhören und einen schönen Tag noch!
example.en: Goodbye, and have a nice day!

mnemonic: AUF (until) + WIEDER (again) + HÖREN (hear) = 'until hearing again' → GOODBYE (on the phone).
AUF (until) + WIEDER (again) + SEHEN (see) = 'until seeing again' → GOODBYE.

example.en: We'll see each other again soon.

mnemonic: BALD sounds like the English word 'bald' — soon you'll go BALD, so act SOON!
BIS (until) + BALD (soon) = 'until soon' → SEE YOU SOON.

example.de: Bis dann, ich muss jetzt los.
example.en: See you then, I have to go now.

mnemonic: BIS (until) + DANN (then) = 'until then' → SEE YOU THEN.

example.de: Bis später, ich melde mich noch mal.
example.en: See you later, I'll get in touch again.

mnemonic: BIS (until) + SPÄTER (later) = 'until later' → SEE YOU LATER.

example.de: Der Preis geht bis zu hundert Euro.
example.en: The price goes up to a hundred euros.

mnemonic: BIS (until) + ZU (to) = 'until to' → UP TO (a limit).
Borrowed straight from Italian — same as English 'ciao': BYE.
DANKE sounds like 'donkey' — imagine a donkey nodding 'THANKS!'.

example.en: Thank you very much for your help.

mnemonic: DANKE (thanks) + SCHÖN (beautifully) = 'beautifully, thanks' → THANK YOU VERY MUCH.

example.en: The bus stop is over there.

mnemonic: DORT sounds like 'dot' — point to a DOT far away: THERE.
DRAUSSEN contains 'aus' (out) — being OUT there means OUTSIDE.

example.de: Ich habe das Buch schon dreimal gelesen.
example.en: I've already read the book three times.

mnemonic: DREI (three) + MAL (times) = 'three times' → THREE TIMES.

example.en: There were three of us traveling together.

mnemonic: DRITT relates to 'drei' (three) — the THIRD one in a group.
GERADE (straight) + AUS (out) = 'straight out' → STRAIGHT AHEAD.
Variant of 'gern' — sounds like 'yearn-eh' — GLADLY, happily.

example.en: Have a nice day! – Same to you!

mnemonic: GLEICH (same) + FALLS (case) = 'in the same case' → LIKEWISE, same to you.
A cheerful Swiss greeting sound — 'GRÜ-etzi!' — casual HELLO.

example.de: Gute Besserung, ich hoffe, es geht dir bald besser.
example.en: Get well soon, I hope you feel better soon.

mnemonic: GUTE (good) + BESSERUNG (improvement) = 'good improvement' → GET WELL SOON.
GUTE (good) + NACHT (night) = literally GOOD NIGHT.
GUTEN (good) + ABEND (evening) = GOOD EVENING.

example.de: Guten Appetit, lass es dir schmecken!

mnemonic: GUTEN (good) + APPETIT (appetite) = 'good appetite' → ENJOY YOUR MEAL.

example.de: Guten Morgen, hast du gut geschlafen?
example.en: Good morning, did you sleep well?

mnemonic: GUTEN (good) + MORGEN (morning) = GOOD MORNING.

example.de: Guten Tag, mein Name ist Herr Müller.
example.en: Good day, my name is Mr. Müller.

mnemonic: GUTEN (good) + TAG (day) = GOOD DAY, a formal hello.
Nearly identical to English 'hello' — same meaning.

example.de: Heute habe ich viel zu tun.
example.en: I have a lot to do today.

mnemonic: HEUTE sounds like 'hoy-tuh' — 'hoy, today's the day!' → TODAY.

example.de: Der Garten liegt hinter dem Haus.
example.en: The garden is behind the house.

mnemonic: HINTER relates to 'hinten' (at the back) — BEHIND something.
Same sound as English 'hurray' — HOORAY!
IMMER sounds like 'ever' — happening forever and EVER: ALWAYS.

example.de: Biegen Sie an der Ampel links ab.
example.en: Turn left at the traffic light.

mnemonic: LINKS looks just like the English word 'links' — golf LINKS curve to the LEFT.

example.de: Mittags esse ich meistens nur einen Salat.
example.en: At noon, I usually just eat a salad.

mnemonic: MITTAG means 'midday' — MITTAGS = 'midday-ly' → AT NOON.

example.en: I would like a glass of water.

mnemonic: A short, punchy northern German greeting — like a quick nod: HI.

example.de: Momentan habe ich sehr viel Arbeit.
example.en: I have a lot of work at the moment.

mnemonic: MOMENT sounds just like English 'moment' — happening right at this MOMENT: CURRENTLY.

example.en: I always drink coffee in the morning.

mnemonic: MORGEN means 'morning' — MORGENS = 'morning-ly' → IN THE MORNING.
NACH (to) + HAUSE (house) = 'to the house' → GOING HOME.

example.de: Deine Kollegen sind alle sehr nett.
example.en: Your colleagues are all very nice.

example.de: Ich habe ein neues Auto gekauft.

mnemonic: NICHT (not) + MEHR (more) = 'not more' → NOT ANYMORE.

example.de: Kannst du das noch einmal wiederholen?
example.en: Can you repeat that once more?

mnemonic: NOCH (still) + EINMAL (once) = 'still once' → ONCE MORE.

example.de: Normalerweise stehe ich um sechs auf.
example.en: Normally, I get up at six.

mnemonic: NORMAL + -ERWEISE (-ly manner) = 'in a normal manner' → NORMALLY.

example.en: We often go to the movies.

mnemonic: OFT looks just like the English word 'oft' (short for often) — OFTEN.
PROST sounds like clinking glasses — 'prost!' at a toast: CHEERS!

example.de: Es gibt viele Geschäfte rund um den Bahnhof.
example.en: There are many shops around the train station.

mnemonic: RUND (round) + UM (around) = 'round around' → AROUND, all over.

example.en: On Saturdays I always sleep in.

mnemonic: SAMSTAG means 'Saturday' — SAMSTAGS = 'Saturday-ly' → ON SATURDAYS.
SCHON (already) + WIEDER (again) = 'already again' → YET AGAIN.
TAT (deed, from 'tun' = to do) + SÄCHLICH (factual) = 'deed-like/factual' → ACTUALLY, indeed.

example.en: I don't have your phone number.

mnemonic: A cheerful, bouncy sound 'chooss!' — casual BYE.

example.de: Das Zimmer ist viel zu klein.
example.en: The room is way too small.

mnemonic: VIEL (much) + ZU (too) = 'much too' → WAY TOO (much).

example.de: Die Praxis ist von neun bis fünf geöffnet.
example.en: The office is open from nine to five.

mnemonic: VON (from) + BIS (until) = literally FROM ... TO/UNTIL.

example.de: Vormittags habe ich meistens einen Termin.
example.en: I usually have an appointment in the morning.

mnemonic: VOR (before) + MITTAG (noon) = 'before noon' → IN THE MORNING.

example.de: Wie bitte? Kannst du das wiederholen?

mnemonic: WIE (how) + BITTE (please) = 'how, please?' → PARDON?
WIE (how) + LANGE (long) = literally HOW LONG.

example.en: How much does the T-shirt cost?

mnemonic: WIE (how) + VIEL (much) = literally HOW MUCH.

example.de: Wie viele Personen kommen zur Party?
example.en: How many people are coming to the party?

mnemonic: WIE (how) + VIELE (many) = literally HOW MANY.
ZU (by) + FUSS (foot) = 'by foot' → ON FOOT.
ZU (at) + HAUSE (house) = 'at the house' → AT HOME.

example.en: First, we need to go shopping.

mnemonic: ZU (to) + ERST (first) = 'to first' → FIRST (of all).

example.de: Zum Schluss möchte ich noch etwas sagen.
example.en: Finally, I'd like to say one more thing.

mnemonic: ZUM (to the) + SCHLUSS (close/end) = 'to the close' → FINALLY, in conclusion.
ZUM (to the) + WOHL (well-being) = 'to your well-being' → CHEERS.
ZURÜCK sounds like 'zoo-ruck' — a boomerang goes out and comes BACK.

example.de: Wir waren zu zweit im Kino.
example.en: There were two of us at the movies.

mnemonic: ZWEIT relates to 'zwei' (two) — the SECOND one in a group.
